formation.explanation: A1: A client proposal is batched by its receiving replica into a local-row instance. Conflict indexes supply sequence/dependencies; thriftiness selects a preferred live peer subset. PreAccept replies are filtered by attempted ballot and phase, then counted/merged. Fast conditions commit directly; otherwise Accept replies at matching ballot establish the coordinator commit threshold. Commit broadcasts carry commands and attributes. Recipients install guarded committed records. Dependency/SCC execution waits for prerequisite commands and committed status, applies ordered operations and answers deferred clients.

context.explanation: A2: Authority is per instance, not exclusive global proposal leadership. Initial ballots equal origin replica ID. Recovery resets bookkeeping while retaining client proposals/value context, selects a ballot, adds a self reply and sends Prepare. Acceptors raise their promise and export prior value ballot/status. The recovering coordinator collects matching replies and selects a highest-value-ballot tuple before committing locally, accepting or restarting phase1. Lower-ballot requests and nonmatching replies are guarded. Complete committed records skip recovery. Master designation affects higher-ballot retry but does not stop other replicas proposing.

connection.explanation: A1/A2 connection: The record status and value ballot exported by Prepare determine whether earlier formation support constrains the new attempt as committed, accepted or merely preaccepted. Reset bookkeeping discards old counts; phase and ballot checks constrain delayed replies. Accepted/committed follower guards limit new PreAccept modifications, while delayed Commit is rejected below a newer promise. Pending local client proposals survive recovery and may be reproposed after NOOP. Execution later consumes the selected record, so retention of support classification matters independently of client visibility.

grounding.derivation: The captured repository presents EPaxos as a corrected replication protocol (M-readme). More concretely, handleAcceptReply declares a command-bearing instance COMMITTED on matching support, handleCommit refuses to replace committed records, recovery has an explicit committed-value preservation branch, and Exec consumes COMMITTED commands as authoritative application inputs. Together these establish the instance decision-agreement responsibility: a later recovery decision cannot substitute a different ordered command batch for an already committed identity. This is a semantic requirement derived from the interfaces and consumers, not an inference that current guards prove it. The check will compare command content, not protocol labels or ballot equality.
grounding.applicability: The launcher uses fixed membership, derives F and disables durability; the constructor enables thriftiness. The contemplated N=5/F=2 history has one crash-stop coordinator and only produced messages. A later-slot Commit supplies the recovery scanner upper bound; omitted elapsed scanning is a substituted legal trigger, not a timing observation.
alternatives: A replica that already knows the first commit is protected by status guards. The intended missing-slot context preserves that guard and tests a different observer.
A changed sequence or ballot alone is not a command-agreement violation.
